english.title: Provide false / misleading information in purported compliance with a Part XI requirement
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in purported compliance with a requirement imposed on you under Part XI of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000,

(A)_[provided information which you knew to be]_
(B)_[recklessly provided information which was]_

false or misleading in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY HOW THE INFORMATION WAS FALSE / MISLEADING..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 177(4) and (5) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes: Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
